title: Role-graph approval flow for canary, A/B, and shadow rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As teams adopt canary, A/B, and shadow traffic patterns for model rollouts, we lack a single, auditable approval surface that maps organizational roles to allowed rollout actions (canary size, canary duration, shadow injection rates, A/B traffic splits) and enforces expiration/delegation semantics. Current options are ad hoc: repo-based PR approvals, manual Slack signoffs, or a central ticket. This causes delays, uneven risk controls, and no cryptographic trace tying approvals to the change that triggered a rollout.

Goal: Design and deliver a Role-Graph Approval Flow in the Redwood Console and API that: (1) maps RBAC groups and individual approvers to specific rollout action scopes, (2) supports temporary delegation with expiry and auto-revocation, (3) requires configurable sign-offs based on risk (canary size > 5% or shadow > 10% triggers Senior Eng + Security signoff), (4) appends a tamper-evident audit entry (signed by KMS) to the rollout event, and (5) surfaces approvals in the rollout UI and audit log export for compliance reviews.

Scope: UX/Console approval flows + API endpoints + backend audit log integration. Out of scope for this ticket: enforcement of approvals for on-prem Private deployments where customer-specific policy engine is used (we will provide hooks and webhooks).

Constraints and considerations:
- Must integrate with existing SSO/SCIM groups and Console RBAC.
- KMS-signing of approval events should be optional per-tenant (default on for Redwood Hosted).
- Approval policies must be evaluable by the rollout controller to permit/deny a rollout attempt programmatically.
- Rollback automation should be able to run independent of human approvals but must record the reason and sign-offs that were present at rollout time.

Success metrics: Reduced mean time to approval for standard low-risk rollouts from current baseline to < 3 hours, adoption by at least two internal teams for a quarter pilot, and audit export format accepted by compliance team for SOC2 readiness.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console: Approval policy UI that lets admins create policies which map RBAC roles/groups to allowed rollout actions and required approver counts.
2) API: endpoints to request approval, approve/reject, and query approval state. All responses include approval event IDs.
3) Delegation: Admins can delegate approval rights for a bounded duration; delegated approvals automatically expire and are rejected after expiry.
4) Enforcement: Rollout controller rejects rollout attempts that lack required approvals; controller returns structured error code (ROLLOUT_APPROVAL_REQUIRED) with link to approval request.
5) Audit: Each approval and final rollout decision is written to audit logs with a KMS-backed signature (or HMAC for tenant opt-out) and is exportable via CSV/JSON in Console.
6) Auto-rollback: When rollout breaches configured quality thresholds and auto-rollback is enabled, rollback is executed and a signed audit entry is emitted stating the trigger and previous approvals.
7) Tests: End-to-end tests cover policy evaluation, delegation expiry, and signed audit generation.
8) Documentation: Docs page with examples for common policies (low-risk, high-risk), and a short how-to for developers to request an approval via API or Console.
tasks: Design: Approval policy data model and UI flows (PM + Design)
Backend: Approval service API (create/request/approve/reject/query) + persistence schema
Auth: Integrate policy evaluator with Console RBAC and SCIM group mapping
Security: KMS signing integration for approval events; fallback HMAC mode for tenant opt-out
Controller: Rollout controller enforcement and structured error paths
UI: Approval request modal, approver dashboard, and policy management screens
E2E tests: Simulate canary and A/B rollouts with missing/present approvals
Docs: Add runbook and compliance export instructions
